threat_event: Business email compromise: a phishing email or an approved MFA push gives an attacker a staff mailbox holding client tax documents; the attacker steals them and sends refund and payment change requests from the firm's address
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Push MFA without number matching; automatic external forwarding allowed; no alerts on inbox rules or risky sign-ins; mailbox logs kept under one year; no phishing training
existing_controls: MFA on the suite and tax software; antivirus; firewall
treatment_plan: Number matching; block automatic external forwarding (done 2026-07-20); suite alerts for inbox rules, forwarding, and risky sign-ins to the Office Manager and MSP; one year of log retention; annual training with quarterly phishing simulations

threat_event: Attacker in a hijacked client email thread, or in the firm's own mailbox, asks the firm to change the direct deposit account on a client's return
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: No call-back verification for bank account changes requested by email or portal message
existing_controls: Preparers usually compare with the prior-year return
treatment_plan: Call-back rule: any change to a refund bank account, address, or email is confirmed by phone on the number on file before the return is transmitted; reviewer checklist item

threat_event: Attacker posing as a client's employee or owner asks the Bookkeeper to change a payroll employee's bank account, diverting wages
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: No call-back verification for payroll bank changes requested by email
existing_controls: Bookkeeper knows most client contacts by voice
treatment_plan: Same call-back rule for payroll bank changes, confirmed with the client's authorized contact on the number on file; training

threat_event: Stolen client data, a stolen PTIN, or the firm's EFIN is used to file fraudulent returns in clients' names
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: No weekly check of returns filed per EFIN and PTIN; no data theft procedure
regulatory_driver: N54-R03 (Pub. 4557 EFIN and PTIN monitoring; Pub. 1345)
existing_controls: PTIN holders review their own annual counts
treatment_plan: Weekly EFIN and PTIN return-count check in season by the Client Services Coordinator; data theft steps in P08

threat_event: Ransomware delivered by phishing encrypts the computers and, through the sync client, the client folders in cloud storage during the filing season
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Desktops sync all client folders; antivirus without behavior-based detection; alerts in business hours only; backup never fully restored
affected_asset_or_process: SYS-03; SYS-06; SYS-08; BP-01 to BP-04
existing_controls: MSP patching and antivirus; firewall; daily suite backup with 1 year of retention
treatment_plan: MSP-managed EDR with alert monitoring; limit sync to the folders each user needs; immutable backup retention confirmed; quarterly full restore tests; training

threat_event: Compromise of the MSP's remote management tool gives attackers control of every computer and the MSP-held administrator logins
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: MSP tool has administrator access to all computers; MSP holds the backup and firewall logins without MFA; MSP contract has no security or breach notice terms
existing_controls: MSP states it uses MFA on its own console (not evidenced)
treatment_plan: Contract amendment: security requirements, breach notice within 72 hours, named technicians, subcontractor list; annual MSP security review with evidence; MFA on MSP-held logins

threat_event: A former employee or seasonal worker signs in to the tax software or email after leaving
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Accounts removed when remembered; the 2026 seasonal assistant's accounts stayed active for 12 weeks (disabled 2026-07-08)
existing_controls: Unique accounts; MFA tied to the user's phone
treatment_plan: Last-day termination checklist; end dates on seasonal accounts; monthly account reconciliation

threat_event: An everyday account with global administrator rights is phished, and the attacker takes over the whole suite tenant
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Owner CPA and Office Manager read email with global administrator accounts
existing_controls: MFA on both accounts
treatment_plan: Separate administrator accounts used only for administration; two sealed break-glass accounts

threat_event: A return or source document sent as a plain email attachment goes to the wrong address or is intercepted
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Returns emailed on client request; no rule blocks unencrypted attachments with SSNs; one misdirected return in 2025
existing_controls: Portal available for delivery
treatment_plan: Portal-only delivery of returns; suite rule that blocks outbound attachments with SSNs unless encrypted

threat_event: A client's portal account is taken over with a reused password and the attacker downloads that client's returns and documents
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Client MFA optional; about 30% of clients use it
existing_controls: Portal lockout after failed sign-ins
treatment_plan: Require client MFA before the 2027 filing season with a help sheet for clients

threat_event: An unencrypted desktop that syncs the client folders is stolen in an office break-in
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: 4 desktops unencrypted; each holds a synced copy of the client folders
existing_controls: Locked suite; after-hours alarm
treatment_plan: MSP enables full-disk encryption on all 4 desktops and reports status monthly

threat_event: Scanned tax documents are recovered from the MFP's internal drive after the leased device is returned
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: MFP keeps scanned images; lease ends 2027-03-31; no wipe requested
existing_controls: None
treatment_plan: Turn on image overwrite now; require a certificate of drive wipe or keep the drive at lease return

threat_event: Staff upload tax return information to the generative AI assistant without an IRC 7216 basis, and the vendor keeps or processes it outside the United States
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: No approved-tools rule; no 7216 analysis; vendor keeps inputs up to 30 days and does not commit to U.S.-only processing
existing_controls: Business plan excludes training on inputs by default
treatment_plan: No client-identifying content in the assistant until counsel confirms a basis (see P10); ask the vendor to delete past uploads; approved-tools rule in POL-04

threat_event: The AI assistant drafts a client letter or IRS notice response with a wrong figure or a nonexistent authority, and it is sent
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: No review checklist for AI drafts
existing_controls: A CPA or enrolled agent signs each letter
treatment_plan: Mandatory check of every cited authority and amount against the source before signing (see P10)

threat_event: A breach exposes former clients' folders kept since 2016, multiplying the number of people to notify and the cost
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: No retention and disposal schedule; about 1,900 former clients still in cloud storage
existing_controls: None
treatment_plan: Retention schedule in POL-04; dispose of former clients' records within 2 years of last use, keeping what law requires; first purge by 2027-06-30

threat_event: The tax software vendor has an outage in the last week before the April or October deadline
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Single SaaS dependency for preparation and e-file
existing_controls: Vendor SOC 2 states RTO 4 hours and RPO 1 hour
treatment_plan: Accepted by the Owner CPA: the vendor meets the BIA, extensions are the fallback, and no alternative vendor is affordable at this size. Revisit if an outage lasts more than one day

threat_event: An internet outage in a deadline week stops access to every SaaS system
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: One internet line; no failover
existing_controls: Owner CPA's phone hotspot
treatment_plan: MSP installs a cellular failover router before the 2027 filing season

threat_event: A hurricane closes the office for several days during extension season
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: No contingency plan; single office
existing_controls: All systems are SaaS and reachable from any location; laptops encrypted
treatment_plan: Short contingency plan: laptops home before landfall, client notice script, early extensions for clients at risk

threat_event: A breach at the tax software, portal, or payroll platform vendor exposes the firm's client data
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Only the tax software vendor's security evidence has been reviewed; no breach notice terms
existing_controls: Tax software SOC 2 report
treatment_plan: Vendor inventory and risk tiering; request security evidence from the portal and payroll vendors; breach notice terms at renewal

threat_event: Data theft is reported late to the IRS, state tax agencies, the FTC, or affected individuals
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: No incident procedure; nobody knew the next-business-day IRS report or the 30-day FTC notice
existing_controls: None
treatment_plan: POL-03 and the P08 runbook; reporting rule in training; tabletop before the filing season

threat_event: FTC enforcement or IRS e-file sanctions after a breach because the written program was out of date and required elements were missing
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: 2024 WISP never updated or followed; no risk assessment before 2026; PTIN renewals affirmed a WISP that was not maintained
existing_controls: Qualified Individual designated 2026-07-06
treatment_plan: Adopt the P06 policies as the WISP; operate the annual cycle; brief preparers before PTIN renewal

threat_event: Client folders or mailboxes cannot be restored after deletion, ransomware, or a malicious administrator
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: No full restore test; one shared MSP administrator account without MFA could delete the backups; immutability not confirmed
existing_controls: Daily suite backup with 1 year of retention
treatment_plan: Full restore test by 2026-09-30, then quarterly; MFA and named MSP accounts on the backup console; confirm immutable retention

threat_event: A staff laptop is lost or stolen
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Laptops leave the office with preparers
existing_controls: All 4 laptops encrypted; MFA on every SaaS system
treatment_plan: Accepted by the Office Manager: data on the laptops is encrypted, which removes it from Florida's definition of personal information (501.171(1)(g)2.) and from the FTC notification event (314.2(m)) unless the key is taken

threat_event: An attacker guesses or reuses the MFP's "scanner" mailbox password, which works without MFA over legacy authentication, or changes the MFP's settings through its default administration password
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Scan-to-email uses an app password over legacy authentication; MFP administration page has the default password (found in P07 testing 2026-08-04)
existing_controls: Firewall blocks inbound access to the MFP
treatment_plan: Change the MFP administration password (done 2026-08-05); move scan-to-email to a send-only connector or scan-to-portal; block legacy authentication tenant-wide

threat_event: MSP technicians and other contractors see tax return information without the written IRC 6713 and 7216 notice, exposing the firm to a 7216 violation
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: No written notice ever given; MSP can open client files on every computer
existing_controls: None
treatment_plan: Written 6713 and 7216 notice signed by each MSP technician and the MFP lessor's service technicians; limit MSP access to what the service needs
